name: r51_reversed_capacity_profile_binding
description: Pair wide and narrow ends of A and D in reversed vertical roles.
mechanism: Bind A wide upper walls to D wide lower walls (red) and A narrow lower walls to D narrow upper walls (blue). Test reversing the vertical direction of cumulative capacity: transfer the high half-volume rise of an upward-flaring vase to the high narrow end of the downward-tapering vase, effectively using empty headspace instead of filled-from-base volume. This predicts D, not a local E-waist minimum.
primary_math_proof: A is uniquely above half height; B,C,E exactly half height by constant section or up/down profile symmetry; D below half height by decreasing section area. Equal capacity is given, so this comparison uses within-vase volume fractions, not absolute silhouette widths.

difference_audit.old: background_17 local_neck_cumulative_volume_confusion paired only A lower stem with E waist; preset E, A/A MISS.
difference_audit.new: Two distributed wide/narrow endpoint correspondences between A and D reverse the vertical volume profile. No E styling, no waterline, no narrowest-local-waist ranking.
difference_audit.substantive_difference: Orientation of full vertical capacity distribution and filled-vs-empty cumulative role; two different receiving regions with opposite height order.
difference_audit.preset_rationale_before_calls: An erroneous integration from the opening downward treats D narrow upper quarter as the capacity-accumulation region and chooses D. This is inconsistent with water being poured into the base.
